newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian partner of Bre-X delays legal proceedings.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian partner of Bre-X delays legal proceedings.

text.p: A local partner of Bre-X Minerals Ltd, majority owner of the spectacular Busang gold find in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province, said he will not file an intended $1.9 billion lawsuit against the Canadian company until December 4.

Jusuf Merukh said Bre-X had asked him to delay his November 22 deadline to negotiate over an ownership dispute because the company was busy, possibly due to talks with gold giant Barrick Gold Corp to exploit Busang, which is estimated to contain 47 million ounces of gold.
Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp said overnight that they were negotiating under the "guidance" of the Indonesian government, which wants them to complete a deal by December 4.
Indonesia wants Toronto-based Barrick to hold 75 percent of Busang while Bre-X keeps 25 percent, Alberta-based Bre-X said.

Bre-X said the Indonesian Mines Ministry "has also advised that the Indonesian government would appreciate if the parties could consider a 10 percent participation being given to the Indonesian government".
Merukh said the talks between Bre-X and Barrick were possibly over a partnership to operate Busang and would not affect his 40-percent ownership claim of the find.
